newsitem.title: USA: US green groups urge halt to salvage logging sales.
newsitem.headline: US green groups urge halt to salvage logging sales.

text.p: A number of environmental and conservation groups urged the Clinton administration to cancel remaining salvage logging rider sales that otherwise still would go through despite the moratorium on new sales announced last week.

"...there remain a number of sales that will be auctioned in the coming two weeks that threaten our national forests and fail to meet your directives to the Forest Service to protect the environment," the organizations wrote President Clinton.
"We therefore urge you to cancel the remaining logging rider sales that threaten our national heritage," the letter signed by 135 national, regional and local organizations said.
The Agriculture Department, which oversees the Forest Service, said Friday it was halting advertisements for remaining sales under the emergency salvage logging rider, which expires December 31.
Sales that had already been advertised but had not yet been auctioned would proceed under that order.
There are about 50 sales that could be auctioned before December 31, Jim Jontz, of the Western Ancient Forest Campaign said.
"As has been the case for most of the year, these sales would log green, healthy forests, many sheltering valuable waterways, fisheries and endangered wildlife," Jontz said.
But the timber industry said the Clinton administration had yielded to environmental extremists "at the expense of responsible management of public forests" when it halted advertising for sales.
